prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: futuristic digital goal replacement concept board for the existing Fuzeball video game.
Input image 1: actual table-goal geometry reference rendered from the game's GLB. Input image 2: assembled in-game table for scale and context. They are geometry references. Keep the walnut table, existing thin rounded brass rectangular front frame, green field, goal cutout and cabinet proportions. Add a futuristic goal device only to this existing table. Be inventive with the digital goal, not with the rest of the table.
Geometry: pitch 120 long x68 wide; goal at x=60, opening 22 wide x10.2 high, goal pocket extends OUTWARD behind it 9 units to x=69, z=-11..11. Preserve this mouth and approximate size envelope. The front opening must be visibly open: ball travels through it freely, into a pocket BEHIND the goal line. Digital surfaces belong on the rear, sides and roof of the pocket, not as an opaque barrier across the front. A small slim dark emitter base may extend beneath the goal pocket beyond the wood, following the existing 9-unit depth. No floating unmounted sci-fi hardware.
Style: convincing high-end real-time game concept render, sophisticated restrained sci-fi, legible at gameplay scale, luminous translucent shaders and convincing light spill on the existing brass and wood. Clearly energy, light and holography; absolutely NO physical net, cord, knots, rope, chain-link or cloth. No ordinary net painted neon. Avoid excessive bloom, blinding white areas, noisy sparks, huge machines, fantasy portals or tunnels to other worlds. The pocket should be visible and the ball trackable through the effect. Keep the cabinet and field natural materials; do not turn the whole table futuristic.
Composition: LANDSCAPE concept sheet with deep charcoal background, tasteful short title along top. One large three-quarter close-up installed on the reference table in left two-thirds, with clear view through open mouth into digital pocket. Right third has two smaller panels: SIDE PROFILE at top showing the actual geometry of this same design at rest; GOAL IMPACT at bottom showing a small foosball contacting its rear field, plus that design's distinctive localized electronic response. All three views must consistently represent the same construction and colors. No paragraph annotations or fabricated dimensions. No watermark. Large polished visuals, modest typography and margins.

Text (verbatim): "01 / HOLOGRAPHIC VEIL".
Design direction: A barely-there digital shell in a softly rounded BOX goal pocket. Cyan and ice-blue translucent smooth holographic rear curtain, roof and sides projected by tiny recessed emitter strips on the back of the existing brass frame and a slim graphite perimeter base behind it. No regular grid: use extremely fine horizontal scanlines, a few faint broken interface dashes near edges, subtle digital shimmer and soft gradients across see-through surfaces. Rear curtain has a slight inward curvature at rest and fluid-like flex when hit, like a weightless sheet of light rather than glass. The big hero shows idle with a very subtle residual wave; the GOAL IMPACT inset shows tight bright concentric cyan ripple rings spreading from the ball, local surface displacement, small pixel flecks fading quickly, no explosion. Elegant, readable and plausible as a game shader; mostly empty transparent space.

Text (verbatim): "02 / FLUX CONTAINMENT BOWL".
Design direction: An organic smoothly curved DIGITAL FORCE FIELD, a transparent bowl-shaped half-bubble behind the rectangular brass mouth. Its D-shaped footprint reaches 9 units deep at centre, returns to the goal posts at sides, and the top transitions in a soft rounded dome inside the goal height. No back frame, no ropes, no grid. Only two small anchored projector pods behind the bases of the posts and a slim curved base rail. The field looks like translucent indigo-violet interference film with electric cyan contour highlights and a luminous rim tracing its continuous curved rear silhouette. Clean glossy energy membrane with huge transparent clear areas and gentle iridescence, not a physical glass aquarium. The impact view shows the small ball pressing a local concavity into this continuous energy bubble, with broad fluid radial compression waves and a brief magenta-to-cyan interference pulse. This must have a very different organic curved silhouette from the box veil.

Text (verbatim): "03 / VOXEL CATCHER".
Design direction: A faceted digital basket built entirely from DISCONNECTED FLOATING HOLOGRAPHIC SQUARE TILES and pixels, projected into the 9-unit rear pocket. The rear is slightly narrower than the mouth; chamfered rear corners give a crisp polygonal basket silhouette. Magenta, violet and cool white edge light, dark transparent interiors. Sparse, staggered, floating glass-light tiles on rear, sides and roof with obvious dark gaps and small depth offsets; no connecting strands, no continuous solid panel, no hexagonal mesh. A slender dark emitter rail under the pocket and discreet nodes tucked behind the existing brass posts project the tiles. Show much of the goal cavity empty so the shape feels digital and light. The impact inset shows only a compact cluster of tiles near the ball displaced backwards and breaking into tiny square particles, then regrouping around a bright pixel shockwave. Keep it an appealing realistic game effect, not a massive blocky wall or Lego structure.

Text (verbatim): "04 / PHOTON RIBS".
Design direction: A goal pocket outlined by a sequence of FIVE TO SEVEN luminous gold-white and warm amber ENERGY ARCS sweeping from small flush emitters along one lower side edge up across the roof and down the opposite side to the base. These arcs are cross-sections spaced along the 9-unit goal depth, each a softly rounded U/arch behind the existing brass front mouth. Bright fine luminous cores inside a translucent energy halo, physically intangible and much thinner than metal tubes. Keep most space between arcs empty with only a whisper of smoky amber field connecting them. At the back a few near-vertical parallel light ribbons form the rear capture boundary, without cross links or any woven pattern. No metal rear cage, no neon tube hardware, no lasers crossing the front mouth. Deliberate rhythm of floating luminous contours forms a futuristic sculptural vault. The impact inset shows nearby rear ribbons bending outward around the ball and a pulse of white-gold light travelling along the arches back to the base emitters, with an elegant electrical waveform rather than an explosion. Distinctive clean amber silhouette suited to the brass trim.
